guide_blurb: The pride does the hunting. The mane does the arguing.
_tuning_notes: Savanna lion, from the Animal Garden - Lion source set (public domain). One maned male per pride is assigned at group spawn, exactly like the gorilla's silverback, and the mane part is only rendered for him — the pride leader is readable at a glance. special.pride_courage is how many pride members it takes before a lion will start on a HEALTHY player; below that it behaves like the leopard and only takes weakened or small prey, which keeps a lone lion from being a savanna death sentence. Fur is a per-individual pick from the textures list. RARITY: tier 'rare' (panda-class weight) with pride 3-4 and nearby_cap 6. BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. unchanged: 0.93x polar bear, already clearly above the leopard. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
